c.tagline: Peru's 'White City', carved from volcanic sillar beneath the cone of El Misti.

taxi.fareNote: Most Arequipa taxis are unmetered, so agree the fare before getting in (short in-town rides run about S/6-10). Uber, InDrive and Cabify all operate and give an upfront price, though driver numbers are lower than in Lima.

emergency.note: 105 reaches the national police; 116/106 is for medical/ambulance (SAMU). Arequipa sits at about 2,335 m, so altitude is gentler than Cusco, but still ascend slowly and hydrate.

avoid.reason: Express-kidnapping via unofficial taxis; caution in the centre at night

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed colonial core built from white sillar volcanic stone, wrapped around the Plaza de Armas, cathedral and Santa Catalina Monastery; best for first-timers who want every major sight, restaurant and bar within walking distance.

Arequipa's oldest quarter, a maze of narrow whitewashed alleys, tiny plazas and viewpoints just north of the centre; photogenic and atmospheric, quieter at night, and popular with travelers who want charm a short walk from the action.

A leafy, upscale residential district across the Chili River, famous for its arched sillar mirador framing El Misti and its traditional picantería restaurants; suits those wanting calm streets, sunsets and classic volcano views.

A quiet, green pocket just south of the centre with mid-range and larger hotels along shaded avenues; good for families and travelers who want to be near the historic core without the crowds and noise.

A modern district on the northern heights with malls, cafes and a scenic plaza and mirador; practical for longer stays, remote work and those wanting contemporary comforts a short taxi ride from the old town.
lodging: Katari Hotel at Plaza de Armas

water.note: Drink bottled or purified water; tap water is not reliably safe for visitors.

transit.pay: Pay the flat fare in cash to the driver or fare collector on board - about S/1 (~$0.30) for a city combi ride. There is no rechargeable transit card; carry small coins.
transit.hours: Combis and micros run roughly 5am to 10-11pm; after that, taxis (agree the fare first) fill the late-night gap.
transit.note: Arequipa has no metro or tram; the compact sillar-white colonial centre is best explored on foot, with combis and taxis covering longer trips and the outer districts of Yanahuara, Cayma and Cerro Colorado.

bus: Combis & colectivos to Yanahuara, Cayma & the outskirts

transit.m: Combi/colectivo from the main road outside the terminal to the center, ~30-40 min
Taxi to Plaza de Armas, 15-25 min

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving ~10% at sit-down restaurants for good service is appreciated.
